_how: Copy a move's stations into a take's stations[]. Replace <word> with the narration word (or seconds), move pos/aim onto your set's anchors, keep the shape (distances, heights, travel, hold). z is up. Top-level items (kicks, ep_dissolves) go at film.json top level.

story_job_menu.HOOK (0-4 s): M02 or M03 on the strange act, then M05 or M04 to reveal the big thing. First flight by 1 s.
story_job_menu.SET UP THE WORLD: M09 along a set line, or M17 top-down then drop; M11 to arrive at the hero.
story_job_menu.TALK / MOCKER: M01 creep, M02 on the angry or smug word, M16 orbit only at the peak.
story_job_menu.ACT / BUILD: M10 attention chain (face, hand, part, result, reaction); M03 into the insert.
story_job_menu.EXPLANATION: M07 into the object, then M06 down the list or M13 along the row; M00 rests only where the picture changes.
story_job_menu.ANALOGY: In with M21 or M20, then M08 one long push; the payoff repeats the same path. M25 to compare two.
story_job_menu.CHANGE OF PLACE / TIME: M20 dissolve while flying, M21 match dissolve, M22 wipe, M07 fly-through.
story_job_menu.CLIMAX: M14 ride with the thing (the film's longest flight), M15 alongside, M23 kick on the hit.
story_job_menu.END: M26 pull back to the calm hero in front of the result, creep in, loop to frame 0.

M00.name: LIVING REST
M00.when: Lip sync lines, a reaction, a counter or calendar ticking, the end of every flight.
M00.numbers: Rest 20-48 % of a film (most 20-28 %). One rest 0.6-3.3 s. Never dead still.
M00.rick_example: Railroads 38.6-41.9: a 3.3 s rest while the rail turns red and the calendar flips.
M00.build: One station with a long hold and a small creep. The change comes from the set (material, counter, decal), not the camera.

M01.name: CREEP IN ON TALK
M01.when: TALK and MOCKER lines, the hero explaining calmly, the smug face at the end.
M01.numbers: Glide speed 0.08-0.25 frame widths per second; 1.2-2.8 s; zoom x1.1-1.25.
M01.rick_example: Town 0.6-1.8: creep in on the two at the button while the line sets the rule.
M01.build: Station with framing M and creep 0.04-0.06. The next station is a small push in on the angry or smug word (M02).
M01.camsafe: Eye level. Two-shot: both faces at least 3/4 to the lens (validate.mjs VIEW_MISMATCH).

M02.name: PUSH IN TO LAND
M02.when: The noun the voice names, the clue, the angry word. His most common move: in all 26 films.
M02.numbers: 89 pure push flights in 25 of 26 films; median 0.6 s, up to 2.9 s; zoom x1.2-2.4.
M02.rick_example: Humans random 32.2-34.5: push in x2 on the coin board to the row of six.
M02.build: Two stations on one line; travel 0.6-1.2 s; the second lands on the word.
M02.camsafe: Stay at head height on the way in; never end with the head cut by the caption band.

M03.name: WHIP PUSH (SNAP IN)
M03.when: ACT: the hero grabs, pours, presses. A punch word. Into an insert.
M03.numbers: 0.6-1.5 s; zoom x3-9; peak speed 2-3x a normal flight.
M03.rick_example: Pink cell 5.3-6.4: whip push x3 down into the paint bowl.
M03.build: Short travel (0.6-0.8 s) with a big distance change; turn on motion blur; follow with a rest. Use kicks only if it hits something.
M03.camsafe: Ends top-down on the prop, so no face in frame: the 10-degree limit does not apply to a P framing without a character.

M04.name: PULL BACK REVEAL
M04.when: TURN ('but...'), the joke, how big the thing is.
M04.numbers: 38 pure pull flights in 18 films; median 0.5 s, up to 2.2 s; zoom x0.3-0.9.
M04.rick_example: Window 2.3-4.4: pull back x0.34 from the detail to the whole scene.
M04.build: Close station, then a wide one on the same line behind it. Put a foreground object between them so the pull has parallax.
M04.camsafe: Keep the hero at the frame's lower third so his feet stay in (frame_checks).

M05.name: PULL BACK + CRANE UP (BIG REVEAL)
M05.when: HOOK reveal, TURN, the danger, the scale of the world. Nearly every film.
M05.numbers: 23 flights in 16 films; median 1.2 s, up to 4.1 s; zoom x0.5-0.6.
M05.rick_example: Sailors 34.3-38.5: 4.1 s pull back + crane up from the deck to the ship in the storm.
M05.build: Second station further back and higher; aim moves UP to the big thing, not down to the hero. Set travel (over 3 s needs an explicit travel).
M05.camsafe: High end has no close face, so the camera may look down; the first station stays at character height.

M06.name: CRANE DOWN THE LIST (READING)
M06.when: EXPLANATION: a list of rules, steps, prices, a mechanism from top to bottom.
M06.numbers: Crane-only flights in 8 films; 1-2.7 s per stretch; zoom about x1.
M06.rick_example: Slots 22.5-25.1: crane down the list of outcomes inside the machine.
M06.build: pos and aim both drop by the same amount (a truck, not a tilt), so the list stays flat to the lens. Highlight the key line when the camera lands.
M06.camsafe: No character in frame; keep the caption band clear of the key line.

M07.name: FLY INTO THE OBJECT
M07.when: EXPLANATION start ('crack it open', 'inside your brain'), PLACE CHANGE into the inside world.
M07.numbers: Slots 4.3 s, zoom x8.9; painkillers 8.7 s, zoom x58.
M07.rick_example: Slots 17.1-21.4: push into the machine and down inside it.
M07.build: Three stations: outside, the opening (hold 0), inside. The opening must be a real hole in the model; or put a 6-10 frame ep_dissolve at the middle station.
M07.camsafe: Do not pass through a character card (FACE_BEHIND).

M08.name: ANALOGY CORRIDOR (ONE-POINT PUSH)
M08.when: ANALOGY ('picture your body as a house'), and its payoff.
M08.numbers: Painkillers 15.0-23.7 (8.7 s) and 25-34 (9.3 s, the same path again). His longest flights.
M08.rick_example: Painkillers 15-23.7: through the front door and down the corridor to the HEAD room, 8.7 s.
M08.build: Straight line, centred vanishing point, doors on both sides. Save the stations; the payoff copies them with the changed set. ep_dissolves at the start.
M08.camsafe: Corridor at eye height; walls must not clip the near plane.

M09.name: TRAVEL ALONG A SET LINE
M09.when: SET UP THE WORLD (who, where, stakes); moving between places that are connected.
M09.numbers: Railroads 3.7-11.5: one 7.8 s flight, 4 places, 0 cuts.
M09.rick_example: Railroads 3.7-11.5: canyon rim, over the edge, across the desert, into the hall, all one flight.
M09.build: Pass-point stations (hold 0) every 2-3 s along the line; build the line as ONE connected set. Needs follow for set lines to make it easy (tool gap).
M09.camsafe: Land at character height when the hero comes into frame.

M10.name: ATTENTION CHAIN
M10.when: ACT / BUILD: the hero makes or uses the thing.
M10.numbers: Cart 17.5-22.7: one 5.3 s flight round the board, the tubes, the strings, his hands, the crowd.
M10.rick_example: Cart 17.5-22.7: board, tubes, strings, hands, crowd in one flight.
M10.build: Short holds (0.3-0.5 s) so it reads as one move. The hand landing is where the props touch (hands on objects rule).
M10.camsafe: Each landing with a face: 3/4 to the lens, eye level; check the middle of each travel too.

M11.name: PUSH + TRUCK ARC (ARRIVE BESIDE)
M11.when: Arriving at a new character or place inside the same set; the most common combined move.
M11.numbers: 78 push + truck flights in 18 films; median 1.1-1.2 s, up to 5.2 s; zoom x1.3-5.
M11.rick_example: Cart 6.0-7.9: push + truck past the front soldiers to the two in the corner.
M11.build: Travel is straight between stations, so an arc needs a middle pass-point (hold 0). Put a foreground object near the first half.
M11.camsafe: The arc changes the view angle of the hero: views come from apply_looks; validate.mjs at 0/25/50/75/100 %.

M12.name: PULL + TRUCK (STEP BACK TO SHOW TWO)
M12.when: Comparison, the rival enters, 'everyone else', after a close moment to show the room.
M12.numbers: 50 flights in 16 films; median 1.3 s, up to 3.9 s; zoom x0.3-0.9.
M12.rick_example: Job Japan 34.1-37.7: pull back + truck from the man at his desk out through the window to the whole building.
M12.build: Two stations; aim also moves toward the second subject so both end in frame.
M12.camsafe: Keep both figures inside the frame edges at the end (frame_checks).

M13.name: LATERAL TRUCK ALONG A ROW
M13.when: Listing items, a crowd of the same people, 'one after another'.
M13.numbers: 27 flights in 12 films; median 1.0-1.2 s, up to 2.9 s; zoom about x1.
M13.rick_example: Second draw 21.9-24.7: truck right beside the cowboy along the row of saloon fronts.
M13.build: pos and aim move by the same vector. Or use drift on a rest for a slow slide.
M13.camsafe: Do not truck behind a character standing in the row (FACE_BEHIND).

M14.name: RIDE WITH THE MOVING THING
M14.when: CLIMAX (the idea works), any 'it flies, it races, it falls'.
M14.numbers: Cart 51.7-55.5 crane up with the spark 3.9 s; coaster 52.3-59.9 up the loop; pirate cannonball 30-31; second draw 0.8-3.5 rides with the bullet; painkillers 6.9-9.5 rides with the pill down the tube.
M14.rick_example: Cart 51.7-55.5: crane up WITH the spark as it splits into 82 flames.
M14.build: Today follow works for characters only. For a prop or effect, key pass-points every 0.5 s along its path (same offset each time), until film_plan.py gets follow for props.
M14.camsafe: Long follows stay at character height, within 10 degrees down.

M15.name: TRACK ALONGSIDE
M15.when: A race, a chase, two speeds compared, the march.
M15.numbers: Mirror 27.5-32.2 beside the horses; coaster 41.4-46.2 slow car then fast car (same move, two speeds).
M15.rick_example: Mirror 27.5-32.2: tracking beside the racing horses.
M15.build: follow with follow_k 1.0 and a side offset; for 'two speeds', copy the same station with the faster runner.
M15.camsafe: Side view needs the side drawing: camsafe gives it; check MEME_SIDE faces.

M16.name: ORBIT ROUND THE SPEAKER
M16.when: MOCKER at its peak, the villain's line, the hero's decision. Never just to decorate.
M16.numbers: Railroads 13.7-19.6: push in, then 3.1 s orbit + crane down while the face goes purple.
M16.rick_example: Railroads 13.6-19.6: push in, then orbit + crane down round the angry boss.
M16.build: Three or more stations on a circle round the face (radius kept). Say the reason in CAMERA_NOTE.md.
M16.camsafe: Max 60-70 degrees round a card; never past side view (camsafe views, VIEW_MISMATCH).

M17.name: TOP-DOWN GOD VIEW + DROP
M17.when: SET UP a place that is a pattern (round town, maze, army), a crowd forming a shape.
M17.numbers: Town 4.5-9.5: top-down over the round town, then down to the centre; 53-55 the crowd from above.
M17.rick_example: Town 4.5-9.5: top-down over the round town, then down to the button.
M17.build: Top-down station needs up [0,1,0] so the heading cannot spin.
M17.camsafe: Characters are tiny from above, fine; the landing is back at character height.

M18.name: HUGE-TINY VERTICAL TILT
M18.when: Scale, effort, 'so tall nobody...', the hero's climb.
M18.numbers: Town 13-15.5 (the ladder); spear 'taller tower'; push + crane up 32 flights in 16 films.
M18.rick_example: Town 13-15.5: the tall ladder with the tiny climber.
M18.build: Crane (move pos up), not only tilt, so the climber stays readable.
M18.camsafe: Low angle on a figure: STEEP/LOW flags in validate.mjs; keep the hero's face visible.

M19.name: POV THROUGH THE OBJECT
M19.numbers: Pirate 25-27 down the cannon; mirror 18 through the telescope ring.
M19.rick_example: Pirate 24.5-27: from the furnace to over the cannon barrel, the gun's view of the gunners.
M19.build: Camera inside or right behind the object; the object's rim is the foreground. A round mask is a 2D overlay.
M19.camsafe: No face close to the lens; check FACE_HIDDEN on the subject.

M20.name: DISSOLVE WHILE FLYING
M20.when: CHANGE OF PLACE or TIME when the places are not connected.
M20.rick_example: Coaster 25.9-30.6: push, dissolve while flying, the same push on up the red carpet.
M20.build: End the old take mid-travel; start the new take mid-travel the same way; ep_dissolves [{at, frames: 8-12}] at the joint.
M20.camsafe: Both takes: character height at the joint.

stations._note: next take starts with the same direction of motion

M21.name: MATCH DISSOLVE (SHAPE TO SHAPE)
M21.when: Analogy start, 'just like...', jump from small to big.
M21.numbers: Sailors 50-53: oil on the soup turns into the calm sea.
M21.rick_example: Sailors 50-53: oil on the soup dissolves into the ocean.
M21.build: Shape centred at the same place in both takes; ep_dissolves 10-14 frames; keep a slow push through the joint.

M22.name: FOREGROUND WIPE
M22.when: Place change in a busy scene, a quick time jump.
M22.numbers: Pirate 48.5-50.6 (the hull passes); railroads train wipe.
M22.rick_example: Pirate 48.3-50.6: the hull passes close and wipes to the next shot.
M22.build: An object moves across close to the lens; cut the take when it fills the frame.
M22.camsafe: The wiping object never passes through a character.

M23.name: IMPACT KICK
M23.when: The smash, the explosion, the bell, the fall.
M23.rick_example: Pirate 6.2-8.7: the smash with a kick, then pull back + truck to the wreck.
M23.build: Top-level kicks [{at, amp}]; only on a real hit.

M24.name: TIPPED SWING (DUTCH IN THE MOVE)
M24.numbers: Sailors 31-34 on the rolling deck; roll up to about 15 degrees; level at every rest.
M24.rick_example: Sailors 31-34: tipped high angle on the rolling deck.
M24.build: Use travel_roll on the move, never roll on a rest (gate: tilt while resting <= 0.5).

M25.name: SAME MOVE, TWO SPEEDS
M25.when: Comparing two options, before and after.
M25.numbers: Coaster 41.4-46.2: slow truck with the slow car, then fast push with the fast car that flips.
M25.rick_example: Coaster 41.4-46.2: slow truck with the slow car, fast push with the fast one.
M25.build: Copy the station block; change only the subject and the travel time.

M26.name: END PULL BACK
M26.rick_example: Cart 64.4-66.8: pull back to the hero in front of the mushroom cloud.
M26.build: Last station loop: true ends on frame 0 (the hook picture).
M26.camsafe: Hero at character height, result behind him, both in frame.
